karmique.introTitle: What kind of bond are you in?
karmique.q1: Think back to the very beginning of your story. How did things get started?
karmique.q1a: Slowly. We got to know each other over weeks, with nothing rushing us.
karmique.q1b: Something clicked instantly, as if this meeting was meant to happen right then.
karmique.q1c: Everything moved far too fast, and I was swept along before I had time to think.
karmique.q2: When you met, did you feel like you already knew this person?
karmique.q2a: No, I simply discovered someone new.
karmique.q2b: Yes, an unsettling familiarity, as if our two stories recognised each other.
karmique.q2c: Yes, and above all the feeling of replaying a scene I had already lived through elsewhere.
karmique.q3: How would you describe the attraction you feel for this person?
karmique.q3a: Strong and calm. It has never made me lose my footing.
karmique.q3b: Magnetic, almost destabilising. It pushed me out of my comfort zone.
karmique.q3c: So irresistible that I overrode everything my judgement was telling me.
karmique.q4: Has your relationship gone through breakups followed by reunions?
karmique.q4a: Never, or just once, and things were said properly.
karmique.q4b: We drifted apart then found each other again, but each separation served a purpose.
karmique.q4c: We leave and take each other back on a loop, always for the same reasons.
karmique.q5: Emotionally, what does this relationship look like day to day?
karmique.q5a: Fairly steady. We have ups and downs like everyone else.
karmique.q5b: Intense, with real jolts, but those jolts moved something in me.
karmique.q5c: Exhausting. I swing from euphoria to anxiety without any control over it.
karmique.q6: After spending a whole evening together, how do you feel?
karmique.q6a: Good. Rested, in the right place, the way you feel after time that does you good.
karmique.q6b: Shaken, with a lot to process, but not unhappy.
karmique.q6c: Drained, as if the evening had taken all my energy.
karmique.q7a: They are rare, and we always end up understanding each other.
karmique.q7b: They touch sensitive spots, but they have moved us forward.
karmique.q7c: It is always the same argument coming back, with the same sentences.
karmique.q8: What does this relationship bring out in you?
karmique.q8a: Mostly the best of me. I feel good about myself when I am with this person.
karmique.q8b: Old wounds I had never had the courage to look at properly.
karmique.q8c: My worst reflexes: jealousy, control, a panicked fear of being abandoned.
karmique.q9: Does this story remind you of a relationship you have already lived through?
karmique.q9a: No, it is like no other.
karmique.q9b: It echoes an old story, but I am going through it differently this time.
karmique.q9c: It is exactly the same pattern as in my previous relationships.
karmique.q10: Do you feel free to leave if you decided to?
karmique.q10a: Yes. I could leave, I simply do not want to.
karmique.q10b: I have thought about it seriously, and that questioning taught me a lot about myself.
karmique.q10c: No. I have already tried several times and I cannot do it.
karmique.q11: What place have the people close to you had since this relationship began?
karmique.q11a: The same as before. My friends and family still have their place in my life.
karmique.q11b: I stepped back from some people, but it was a choice I stand by.
karmique.q11c: I cut myself off from almost everyone because of this relationship.
karmique.q12: What do the people close to you say when you talk about your relationship?
karmique.q12a: That they think you look good together.
karmique.q12b: That they can see me changing, sometimes with worry, sometimes with admiration.
karmique.q12c: What they have been telling me for a long time: this relationship is hurting me.
karmique.q13: How does your body react to this story?
karmique.q13a: Without any drama. I sleep well and I feel no particular tension.
karmique.q13b: I went through some restless stretches, then things settled down.
karmique.q13c: Knots in my stomach, sleepless nights, and I watch my phone constantly.
karmique.q14: Can you picture a future with this person?
karmique.q14a: Yes, we talk about it calmly, without making it dramatic.
karmique.q14b: I do not know where this is taking us, and I have learned to live with that uncertainty.
karmique.q14c: Impossible. We do not even know whether we will still be together in a month.
karmique.q15: How is the effort shared between the two of you?
karmique.q15a: Fairly evenly. Each of us gives and each of us receives.
karmique.q15b: I gave a great deal, and I eventually understood why I needed to.
karmique.q15c: I feel like I owe this person something, without being able to say what.
karmique.q16: After a crisis, how does making up go?
karmique.q16a: We talk it through, we apologise, and the matter is settled.
karmique.q16b: Every reconciliation has taken us one step further.
karmique.q16c: It is very intense, then everything starts again a few days later.
karmique.q17: How do you feel when this person goes quiet on you?
karmique.q17a: Nothing in particular. I know they will come back to me.
karmique.q17b: It confronts me with my own difficulty being alone, and that is instructive.
karmique.q17c: An anxiety I cannot control, which takes up all the space.
karmique.q18: Since this relationship began, have you changed?
karmique.q18a: I have stayed myself, with one more person by my side.
karmique.q18b: I am not quite the same person any more, and I do not regret it.
karmique.q18c: I no longer recognise myself, and I do not like it at all.
karmique.q19: Deep down, what keeps you in this relationship today?
karmique.q19a: Being happy with this person, quite simply.
karmique.q19b: The feeling that something between us is not finished yet.
karmique.q19c: The thought of losing them, which terrifies me more than the relationship hurts me.
karmique.q20: If you could go back, would you live this story again?
karmique.q20b: Yes, knowing in advance that it would be demanding.
karmique.q20c: I do not know, and that question tightens my stomach.
karmique.pf_apaise_d: Your answers do not describe a karmic relationship. They describe a bond that stands on its own: you feel safe, conflicts get resolved, and the intensity you experience is not paid for in anxiety. In spiritual vocabulary this is closer to what people call a soulmate: a relationship that builds rather than tests. You stay because you are happy, not because you cannot leave, and that is the whole difference.
karmique.pf_apaise_a: Do not go looking for turbulence where there is none. Many people confuse intensity with depth and end up worrying about how calm their relationship is. A relationship that does not hurt is not a dull relationship: it is a working one. Keep nurturing what makes it safe, above all the ability to say anything without fearing the other person's reaction.
karmique.pf_echos_d: Your bond is not entirely karmic, but it carries the echoes of one. Some of your answers point to repetition: an argument that always comes back identical, a pattern you already know, moments where you give more than you receive. The rest of the relationship stays balanced and does you good. In other words, there is indeed something to untangle between you, but it has not yet spread to the whole of your story.
karmique.pf_echos_a: Name the loop precisely. Identify the argument that always plays out the same way and write down how it unfolds: what sets it off, what each of you says, how it ends. Once it is down in black and white, it loses much of its mystery. This is the ideal moment to talk about it together, while the relationship is still solid enough to take the conversation.
karmique.pf_karmique_d: Your answers tick most of the markers attributed to karmic relationships: an attraction that short-circuited your judgement, breakups followed by reunions, the same argument going round in circles, and the distinct feeling of replaying a story you have lived before. You stay less out of happiness than out of an inability to leave. This is exactly what spiritual tradition describes as a debt to be settled, and what psychology calls, more prosaically, an attachment kept alive by alternating warmth and coldness.
karmique.pf_karmique_a: Hold on to one thing: intensity is not proof of love, and a lesson that costs you your health is not a lesson. You owe no debt to anyone. Start with the most concrete step: for three weeks, write down how you feel after each moment spent together, then read it back with a cool head. And if your relationship involves fear, control or humiliation, this is no longer a question of karma: our toxic relationship test and our narcissistic partner test exist for exactly that.
karmique.pf_miroir_d: Your relationship shakes you without destroying you, and that is what sets it apart from a karmic bond. It has confronted you with things you were avoiding, it has taken you through separations, but each of them served a purpose and you came out of it changed. This is the profile that spiritual vocabulary associates with the twin flame: a bond that acts as a magnifying mirror on what you have to work through. The difference from a karmic bond comes down to one word: here, things move forward.
karmique.pf_miroir_a: Make the most of what this mirror shows you, but do not mistake growth for endurance. A relationship that helps you grow leaves you stronger after each trial, not more tired. Ask yourself the question every six months: am I doing better than before? If the answer stays yes, the bond is doing its work. If it turns to no, that is the sign the relationship has gone from mirror to loop.
